posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Mint.

Kaarga games are usually a damage race. Not because you want to kill targets, but because that’s what gains tokens. Doing lots of AoE makes the crowd happy.

So this setup is all about Action Stuntman, because he’s the only one that can really do that quickly. Captain Cosmic needs time to build, and Xtreme Captain Cosmic is slower than the other versions at doing so, since he doesn’t get his extra card play from his base power. Bunker is another slow setup, and while starting with a grenade launcher helps, he can’t do the 2 points to 3 targets required here without some damage boost that he isn’t going to get. Tempest can pull it off if he draws Hailstorm, but he didn’t in my game.

Stuntman did almost all of this himself, and I didn’t lose anyone. He just kept pulling ridiculous strings of attacks, mostly blowing things up with mines, since he starts with 2. Sure, “I do all my own stunts” is bad for the heroes too when he’s dropping mines, but as long as he’s doing a lot more damage to the villains than the heroes, this works for Warfang. It’s great with “No Time to Bleed,” as well.

I won on round 4. Kaarga was flipped and I had 25+ crowd favor. I completely lost track of all the stuff Stuntman was doing on Kaarga’s turn to knock her down. It went something like: Stuntman takes damage, Moving Target lets him use a power, he uses All My Own Stunts to play The Usual Solution, damages Kaarga, she retaliates with 1 psychic damage to everyone due to The Mindbreaker title, which also means everyone takes +2 damage on the next attack because of the Seeker title, he shoots her due to No Time to Bleed, a mine goes off, Stuntman gains The Champion for nuking a bunch of constructs, Stuntman tries to shoot himself because of the mine and No Time to Bleed, but since it’s 5+ damage he destroys it and shoots Kaarga with his machine pistol instead,  and then finishes her off with Coup Vexant.

Seriously, one way or another he did something like 20+ damage to Kaarga during her turn. The +2 damage to each attack from a couple of All My Own Stunts had a lot to do with that.

Minty goodness but I can't tell you how.

What I can tell you is that it was, appropriately, the Stuntman Show.

Still not familiar enough with Stuntman to know the exact combinations flying out fast and furious, but going in to this one-shot I knew enough about Stuntman to know that with any damage boosts, he goes nuts. Since his variant gives him that as a base, ALL OF THE DAMAGE for my game came from Stuntman. It got even worse once he picked up the Seeker title. Sure, Captain Cosmic pew-pew'ed a couple measly lasers and Bunker tossed a couple grenades, but seriously. Tempest was just there to keep the worst gladiator's end of turn effects from happening it seemed like. CC's constructs distracted the "target lowest" gladiators, Bunker.... bunkered I guess, and Stuntman blew up the Arena several times over.

Ended with Stuntman at the lowest at 6 and everyone else around 10, favor something like 22-13

 

~Komori

posts.cooked:
Same deal here: Mint, 28-7, the Stuntman Show.

Round 1: Stuntman does some training and puts out a couple of cards.  CC double-skips because the only other thing he could do is play a construct, and with 4 damage on the table headed to the hero with the lowest HP, that would have been a free point.  Bunker plays and fires the grenade launcher.  Tempest just puts down his Resilience, since he can't do damage and is scheduled to take some.

Round 2: Stuntman plays some more stuff, including smashing the Celestial for Death-Caller.  CC goes ahead and plays, but that meant Bunker had to skip his attack or Tarnis would have gotten Mindbreaker.  Tempest double-skips.

Round 3: Kaargra pisses Stuntman off, who murders everything and earns 5 titles.  Game ends at the start of Captain Cosmic's turn, with Death-Caller bypassing Kaarga's Unbreakable.

I could have literally double-skipped with everyone but Stuntman every turn and had basically the same result.  Good lord, he gets stupid.

posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
When I see Kaarga as a one-shot, I just assume I’m going to end up with Fine because there are so many ways to lose that are unpredictable. For example you can be close to a victory and have Fickle Fans lose the game for you. Whatshername the Adept scores 3 crowd points every turn, which is a serious timer. The titles can turn assets into liabilities - having any kind of damage resistance is bad if The Seeker is still available as a title.

Kaarga’s one of those villains that practically demands control of the villain deck via Infrared Eyepiece or Extrasensory Perception, but heavily penalizes support characters because they’re not doing damage, and not doing damage means losing the crowd favor race.

So yeah, I was surprised to get Mint, and surprised at how much Action Hero Stuntman could chain together attacks and damage bonuses. I’ve been playing with Stuntman a lot recently, and I was aware of the sort of out-of-turn shenanigans he does, but getting 3 extra plays in a round was more than I usually see.

posts.cooked:
Pretty easy mint with everyone still in the high teens. 21-10. Stuntman doing most of the heavy lifting (as well as all his own stunts!). I was winning pretty handily, but had a pretty crazy mine go off in the last round that essentially gave 3 titles to Stuntman and triggered a power usage for him, which pretty handily cleared Kaargra out.

Probably one of the more relaxing games I’ve had against Kaargra - I enjoy her fight, but I do think it’s one of the easier ones to lose, as the wrong order of a few random cards can have a big impact on you, but in this case Stuntman was just putting consistent damage across the whole area and it was her and the Gladiators who were struggling to keep up.

posts.name: rjc917
posts.cooked:
I just played a practice game since I don't think I've ever done Challenge Kaargra before.  I discovered there are some really nasty Gladiator-Title combinations!

S'sdari with Death Caller means any constructs you play are immediately killed.  But worse than that is Provocator Tarnis with Chaos Lord.  Every turn he's dealt damage, you play a villain card.  And he redirects the first damage dealt to a villain each turn to himself.  So any turn you damage a villain, a new villain card gets played.

I got lucky with a Fickle Fans and had a chance to win if I could just finish off Kaargra, but Stuntman went a bit overboard with his stunts and his mines killed all of his teammates (except the Unbreakable Bunker!) as well as the Representative of Earth.
